title: Build installable JSIMPLIFIER backend suite
description: Create an in-repo installable JSIMPLIFIER-style static pipeline backend because the public research signal does not yet provide a stable backend install target.
scope: JSIMPLIFIER worker implementation, Docker packaging, tests
action: Implement a bundled static JSIMPLIFIER worker wrapper and Docker fragment so `jsimplifier.pipeline.run` has a real backend even before a stable upstream release exists.
implementation: Build an in-repo static pipeline worker with deterministic passes: parse/profile, literal normalization, string-array recovery handoff, control-flow flattening hints, and artifact emission.
Expose the worker through `JSIMPLIFIER_WORKER_PATH` with a Docker default under `/opt/rikune-backends/jsimplifier/bin/jsimplifier-worker`.
Keep mode external-compatible through backend-worker.v1 JSON stdin/stdout.
Do not execute JavaScript, call browsers, use Node VM, or call LLM services.
Add fixture tests for success, unsupported input, timeout, malformed output, and readiness.

criteria: `jsimplifier.pipeline.run` can run external mode against the installed wrapper.
Docker dry-run reports `jsimplifier` as installed by an in-repo backend route.
Output includes pass timeline, metrics, artifacts, warnings, and execution_semantics.
Tests prove no dynamic JS execution path is used.
convergence.verification: npm test -- --runTestsByPath tests/unit/jsimplifier-worker.test.ts tests/unit/backend-install-contract.test.ts && npm run docker:generate -- --dry-run
convergence.definition_of_done: JSIMPLIFIER becomes part of our own installable static deobfuscation suite instead of remaining a plan-only research placeholder.

risks: Calling this JSIMPLIFIER can overpromise parity with the paper; label it as JSIMPLIFIER-style until a stable upstream backend exists.
Static-only implementation must not quietly grow dynamic execution stages.
findings: Added JSIMPLIFIER static worker wrapper, Docker fragment, default install route, and worker-backed tool metadata.
